edges.description: Preferential runoff into the low-resistance fistula steals flow from the distal coronary bed, so perfusion of myocardium supplied beyond the fistula origin falls.
A large left-to-right shunt volume-loads the receiving chamber, and the resulting chamber enlargement and eccentric remodeling progress to the congestive heart-failure syndrome.
Chronic chamber enlargement and regional ischemia together provide the structural and electrical substrate for the arrhythmias reported in this disease.
Steal-mediated hypoperfusion of the distal myocardium is felt as ischemic chest pain, typically on exertion when demand rises.
When the perfusion deficit is severe or prolonged, the ischemic myocardium infarcts, which is why infarction appears among the presentations of this disease.
Raised filling pressures and pulmonary venous congestion from the volume-loaded ventricle are experienced as breathlessness.
